subject: Mathematics
title: Dolls!... Dolls!
subtitle: Adding and taking away up to 20
hero_picture: A Kerala seaside road: a father and his son and daughter pushing a wooden cart full of colourful handmade dolls home after selling them, a ship on the sea behind.

sections.heading: Making dolls
text: Pooram is in two days! Sebi and Joji make dolls.
First day: Sebi made 12, Joji made 6.
sections.caption: Making dolls together
sections.picture: A Kerala family sitting together on a mat making colourful dolls by hand: grandfather, mother, father and children, many finished dolls in a heap.

sections.heading: Make a ten
text: Second day: Sebi made 7, Joji made 11.
Making a ten first makes adding easy.
sections.caption: Doll boxes in stacks
sections.picture: Two neat stacks of doll boxes on a table: one stack of 10 boxes and another stack of 8 boxes beside it.

sections.heading: Dolls sold
text: Take away to find how many are left.
sections.caption: Selling the dolls
sections.picture: Two children selling dolls at a stall; a customer buying two dolls, a few dolls left on the shelf.

sections.heading: Prices in order
text: Find the highest price and the lowest price.
Arrange them from lowest to highest.
sections.caption: Dolls with prices
sections.picture: Dolls on a shelf each with a blank price tag (no numbers or letters), a girl arranging them from small to big.

sections.heading: Lime juice
text: A big glass of lime juice is 10 rupees. A small glass is 5 rupees.
One big glass costs the same as two small glasses!
sections.caption: Lime juice prices
sections.picture: A girl at a juice stall with one big glass and two small glasses of lime juice on the counter.

rhyme: Twelve little dolls on a cart,
Six were sold, right from the start,
Twelve take six, how many stay?
Six little dolls to sell today!
activity: Take 15 buttons. Give away some and count how many are left. Write it like 15 − 4 = 11.
talk: How many dolls did Sebi and Joji make on the first day?
Which is easier to add first, the ten or the ones?
summary: To add, make a ten first; to find what is left, take away.

questions.prompt: 12 dolls; 6 were sold. How many are left?
A small glass of juice is 5 rupees. Two small glasses cost?
